senses.gloss:
anṛta
(‘the not-straight)
------------------------------------------
The words ṛta, सत्य and अनृत are frequently used in the Vedic literature, the first two being often used synonymously. If ṛta stands for ‘what is straight,’ the Truth at its fundamental causal level, for the thing—in—itself, सत्य stands for the verbal expression of the same. अनृत which may mean the opposite of ṛta or simply what is not ṛta is used mostly to indicate untruth, commonly called असत्य. Speaking अनृत has always been considered as a great sin.
See also ADHARMA, ASATYA, DHARMA, ṚTA and SATYA.
